title: 해양경비법 시행규칙 / queue:ARTICLE:2:0:00003:part:1/1
full_text:
Article 2 (Order of Measures to Protect Maritime Navigation)
① When a maritime police officer takes measures to protect maritime navigation in accordance with Article 14(1) to (3) of the Act, they must follow the following order: <Amended February 11, 2014, November 19, 2014, July 26, 2017, April 20, 2026>
1. Warning: To the captain (including the person operating the vessel) of a vessel that is performing any of the acts specified in each item of Article 14(1), a warning must be issued regarding the need to cease the act and the consequences of not following the instructions of the maritime police officer to move, disperse, or evacuate, as well as the penalties that apply.
2. Movement, Dispersal, and Evacuation Orders: In addition to the warning in item 1, if the act specified in each item of Article 14(1) is not stopped, or if there is a significant risk of harm to human life or body, or serious property damage, or marine pollution, as stipulated in Article 14(2), the vessel must be moved, dispersed, or the captain, crew, or passengers must be ordered to evacuate, at least three times.
3. Implementation of Movement, Dispersal, and Evacuation:

In the event of non-compliance with the orders for movement, anchoring, or evacuation issued in the second paragraph, the relevant authorities shall directly move or anchor vessels, or evacuate the captain, crew, or passengers.

② When maritime police officers take protective measures as described in the first paragraph, they should do so within the minimum necessary scope. (Amended February 11, 2014, November 19, 2014, July 26, 2017)
